signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Slips ~2.2% to ~$57.7 as hot PCE lifts the USD; caught between a one-year-high 10Y and the sticky-inflation/war premium
signals.detail: Silver spot ~$57.7 after a ~2.2% Friday drop; gold ~$4,054; 10Y at a one-year-high ~4.75% (2Y ~4.28%); DXY ~99.8; September-hike odds HIKE-biased (~60-80% across feeds). Levels as of the Fri 31 Jul US close; metals shut over the weekend
signals.takeaway: The book's single most important line item came off its highs into the weekend: Friday's hot core-PCE + stronger spending lifted the USD to a 3-week high and pulled silver down ~2.2% to ~$57.7 and gold ~1.5% to ~$4,054 — a real-rate/dollar pullback, not a thesis break, with both still near multi-year/record ground. Silver is in a two-sided pull: a hawkish Fed, a one-year-high 10Y (~4.75%) and a hike-biased September are the bearish real-rate channel, while the inflation/war premium (Hormuz LNG-tanker strike 1 Aug) is the bullish one. Structural deficit thesis holds (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit). Silver's larger drop vs gold is the higher-beta tell — hold the core and hedge the silver-vs-gold spread rather than adding leverage into a hot-PCE, strong-dollar tape.

signals.name: Crude oil / Energy
signals.label: Qatari-LNG tanker struck in Hormuz on 1 Aug; US-Iran pause stays BROKEN (Brent ~$90, WTI ~$85)
signals.detail: Brent ~$90.12, WTI ~$84.67 (Fri 31 Jul close); a Qatari-LNG carrier (Gaslog Shanghai) was struck transiting Hormuz on 1 Aug and Iran claimed it stopped two vessels/turned four back; strait near-shut (~4-10 transits/day); a 10-day ceasefire is floated but Iran denies agreeing
signals.takeaway: The dominant cross-portfolio driver stays flipped: over the weekend a Qatari-LNG tanker was struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz (1 Aug) — with Iran separately claiming interdictions — after prices had fallen >5% on the week on de-escalation hopes; the strike firmed oil (Brent ~$90) and kept the pause collapsed (the strait is near-shut) even as mediators float a 10-day truce Iran denies agreeing to. Double-edged for the book: it re-arms the inflation/rate-hike fear pressuring the rate-sensitive core (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech, crypto) as the Fed stays hawkish, but restores the geopolitical bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Trade the escalation-vs-de-escalation odds; the Red Sea/Hormuz front is the live risk, but don't chase the spike given OPEC+ spare capacity.

signals.name: US Treasuries / rates
signals.label: Sticky core PCE (+3.3%) validates the hawkish Fed; 10Y at a one-year-high ~4.75%; September-hike odds stay HIKE-biased
signals.detail: Fed held 3.50-3.75% (three hike dissents, Chair Warsh); June core PCE +3.3% y/y + stronger spending, Q2 GDP +1.5%; 10Y ~4.75% (one-year high, Fri 31 Jul), 2Y ~4.28%; September-hike odds HIKE-biased (CME FedWatch feeds read ~60-80% for a 25bp hike; year-end dot ~3.8%)
signals.takeaway: The data validated the hawkish hold and the bond market kept selling even as stocks made records: June core PCE stayed sticky at +3.3% y/y (headline +3.7%) with stronger personal spending, while Q2 GDP slowed to +1.5% — a stagflation-lite mix that vindicated the three FOMC hike dissents and pushed the 10Y to ~4.75%, its highest in over a year, by Friday's close. September-hike odds stay HIKE-biased (feeds range ~60-80%) — the direct higher-for-longer headwind for the book's highest-beta pain (levered silver, gold miners) and S-REITs, and it lifted the USD to a 3-week high (DXY ~99.8), knocking the metals off their highs. The big USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as productive dry powder. Duration got no bid even on the growth slowdown — favor the belly/quality IG over the long end until the data genuinely softens; Fri's July jobs report (7 Aug) is the next tell.

signals.name: Gold / gold miners
signals.label: Slips ~1.5% to ~$4,054 as hot PCE lifts the USD, but holds near a record; largest weekly fund inflow since April
signals.detail: Gold ~$4,054 after a ~1.5% Friday drop on a firmer USD (was ~$4,080 mid-week); gold funds +$2.0bn (wk to 22 Jul, largest since April). Levels as of the Fri 31 Jul US close
signals.takeaway: Gold came off its highs into the weekend — a ~1.5% Friday dip to ~$4,054 as the hot PCE lifted the USD to a 3-week high — but it held far better than the beta names and stays near a record, with sticky 3.3% core PCE, the Hormuz LNG-tanker strike and multi-month central-bank buying an inflation/haven floor that cushions rising real rates. It drew the largest weekly gold-fund inflow since April (+$2.0bn). Favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage as the steadier metals hold and the cleaner hedge against the Iran pause staying broken — gold fell only ~1.5% vs silver's ~2.2%; BofA's flagged elevated net-longs are the near-term warning.

signals.name: Semiconductors / AI-capex
signals.label: Semis REBOUND as AWS +37% and the $720-745bn hyperscaler capex guide re-validate AI-capex; Burry adds to his Micron short
signals.detail: AMZN +15% (Fri 31 Jul) on AWS +37% to $42.2bn, capex raised ~$220bn; the four hyperscalers now guide to $720-745bn of 2026 capex; MSFT +15% (Thu); Burry disclosed adding to his MU short 24 Jul (per-share short price unverified this run)
signals.takeaway: The AI-chip narrative reversed hard: after >$1trn was wiped since 24 Jul, Amazon's AWS +37% blowout (+15% on 31 Jul) and the combined $720-745bn hyperscaler 2026 capex guide — plus Microsoft's ~15% Thursday gain — re-validated the AI-infrastructure spend, and semis rebounded with the Nasdaq into records. A relief for the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core. But Michael Burry disclosed adding to his Micron short (24 Jul; per-share short price unverified this run) inside an expanded NVDA/MU/SOXX bear book arguing the group sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band — the standing warning that the rebound runs into rich multiples. Favor the internet/platform names (Tencent, Xiaomi) as the core; treat the chip leg as higher-beta and two-sided.

signals.name: Rare earths (ex-China basket)
signals.label: Lynas makes first ex-China terbium; MP/USAR on China entity list; 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff nears
signals.detail: Energy Fuels (UUUU) began building a commercial-scale HEAVY-REE plant at White Mesa on 29 Jul (Tb/Dy/Sm/Eu/Gd, circuits by end-2027); Lynas first commercial-scale terbium oxide outside China + Seadrift TX DoD-funded plant; MP & USAR on China dual-use entity list (22 Jun); China heavy-REE exports still ~50% below pre-control levels; broad MOFCOM controls SUSPENDED to 10 Nov 2026
signals.takeaway: The China/US rare-earth decoupling structurally favors the ex-China watchlist, and it got a fresh, dated catalyst: Energy Fuels started constructing a commercial-scale HEAVY-REE separation plant at White Mesa on 29 Jul (heavy REEs — Tb/Dy — are the China chokepoint), while Lynas advanced ex-China terbium and its DoD-funded Seadrift plant, and MP carries DoD backing (~15% stake, $110/kg NdPr floor). But MP and USA Rare Earth sit on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun) and the broad October-2025 MOFCOM controls are suspended only until 10 Nov 2026 (~3 months out) — the calendar catalyst; China's heavy-REE exports remain ~50% below pre-control levels. This stays a strategic optionality play on the controls snapping back, not an immediate momentum trade: accumulate MP and government-backed UUUU on weakness into that 10 Nov cliff (the early-July UUUU insider open-market buying at $12.70-13.08 is the validated reference band).

signals.name: Tencent / HK tech
signals.label: Tencent suspends buyback into a 12 Aug-results blackout; internet sleeve still favored over the SMIC chip leg
signals.detail: Tencent buybacks (1.1M sh/HK$500.7M on 9 Jul) SUSPENDED from ~22 Jul into a 30-day blackout ahead of 12 Aug results; record China inflow (+$21.3bn) the prior week; Xiaomi buyback 3.9M sh/HK$100.7M (15 Jul)
signals.takeaway: The HK-tech core's internet names had been decoupling from the global chip rout and drew a record China weekly inflow (+$21.3bn) under the 24 Jul Politburo H2-stimulus signal — but Tencent has now suspended its near-daily buyback from ~22 Jul, entering the customary blackout ahead of its 12 Aug interim results, temporarily removing a mechanical corporate bid into a jittery, post-FOMC tape. Xiaomi's own buyback continues. Favor Tencent/Xiaomi (internet/consumer) over the SMIC chip leg while the AI-capex unwind runs, but don't add aggressively before the 12 Aug print; a hawkish Fed (10Y 4.73%) is the near-term beta headwind, and the pre-selloff China inflow (+$21.3bn record week) needs the delayed week-to-29-Jul Flow Show to confirm it held.

congress.deepDive: A fresh exit from the semis leader during the AI-capex-peak scare that has since partly reversed. Sits opposite the Micron/AI bulls (Newhouse) and alongside Burry's standing chip shorts — the congressional book splitting on the AI-capex debate. A direct read-through to the SMIC chip leg of the HK-tech core, which the AWS/MSFT rebound has relieved near-term.

The META/MSFT legs land right into their post-close prints (MSFT +3% AH, META -7% AH). Lands the same day as Liccardo's NVDA sell, capturing the two-sided AI-capex debate within Congress.

The BABA sale is the notable line given the HK-tech book — a member trimming China internet even as the Politburo-stimulus flows bid it. A diversified rebalance rather than a single directional call.

A rare direct overlap with the portfolio's PM-miner sleeve, and well-timed as oil re-spiked ~8% on the Iran-pause breakdown.

The Intel leg lands as INTC restructures under state/government-backstop chatter; the Uber leg extends the household's mega-cap tech/mobility tilt. No new Pelosi PTR has surfaced since — this remains the freshest trackable trade.

superInvestors.name: Scion / Michael Burry (personal)
superInvestors.rationale: Having deregistered Scion with the SEC in late 2025 (now publishing on Substack), Burry trades personally and discloses only via the newsletter — his last 13F (Q3 2025) held NVDA/PLTR puts (~80% of the book), and he has since expanded chip shorts (NVDA, MU, SOXX, TSLA, CAT), disclosing on 24 Jul that he ADDED to his Micron short (a per-share short price of '$933.86' circulated in a secondary snippet but the source page was not openable this run, so it is left UNVERIFIED/omitted). He argues the SOX sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band. Separately he TRIMMED (did not cover) his Palantir short with PLTR in the $112-118 range (range as stated, an accumulation band not a single-day print) after the 1 Jul Nvidia partnership.
superInvestors.deepDive: The cleanest smart-money expression of the AI-capex-peak thesis — but it is now under pressure: after the semis complex shed >$1trn from 24 Jul, Thursday's Amazon AWS +37% blowout and raised ~$220bn capex, plus Microsoft's record one-day gain, re-validated AI spend and rebounded the chips (Nasdaq +2.8%). His fresh 24 Jul MU short (per-share price unverified this run) sits directly opposite Tepper's big Micron weight and the crowded AI-infra longs (Ackman MSFT, Bridgewater, Tiger) — the marquee two-sided AI debate. No 13F any longer — the newsletter is the only window; self-reported, sizes approximate, not SEC filings.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.value: AAPL+GOOGL now ~30% of the equity book
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire's Q1 13F nearly tripled its Alphabet stake to ~57.8M shares (~$16.6B) while cutting Chevron ~35%, cutting Constellation Brands ~95%, and fully EXITING Visa, Mastercard, UnitedHealth and Amazon — a decisive quality-AI tilt under Greg Abel alongside a continued record cash build (~$397B at Q1-end).

A striking contrast with Duquesne's Q1 GOOGL exit. Q2 13F due 14 Aug — confirm the sell-streak and any new adds then.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Bill Ackman's Q1 13F (filed 15 May, ~$13.7B, top-3 Brookfield/Amazon/Uber ~51%) added a new Microsoft stake, built by end-May to ~$2.4B (funded by trimming Alphabet), and lifted Amazon to ~$2.4B (now 2nd-largest). He has said he initiated FOUR new positions to be revealed in the Q2 report, and continues building Howard Hughes (~46.9%) as a 'modern Berkshire'.
superInvestors.deepDive: The new MSFT stake (~5.65M sh, instantly his #4 at ~15% of the book) looks well-timed after Microsoft's record one-day market-value gain on 30 Jul; Amazon remains a crowded whale consensus (also top for Tepper) and jumped ~9% AH on the AWS +37% beat. The four teased positions plus the Pershing Square USA IPO prep make his 14 Aug 13F one of the most-watched of the cycle. He slashed Alphabet ~95% in Q1 — the opposite of Berkshire's aggressive GOOGL add.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: David Tepper's Q1 book (filed 15 May, ~$5.93B / 31 positions) is led by Amazon (~15%), Micron (~9.5%), Alphabet, Uber and TSM; he added heavily to memory (Micron) and kept 'buy China' (Alibaba top, KWEB add). No July 13D/13G surfaced — carried pending the 14 Aug Q2 13F.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tepper's Amazon conviction makes it the single most-consensus mega-cap long across the tracked whales (also top for Ackman) — vindicated by AMZN's ~9% AH pop on the AWS +37% blowout (30 Jul). His big Micron weight sits directly opposite Burry's fresh 24 Jul MU short; the pair is the sharpest memory-cycle bull/bear split as chips rebounded on the AI-capex re-validation. His only new Q1 position (SanDisk) was also initiated by Druckenmiller — a quiet two-whale memory bet.

superInvestors.rationale: Chase Coleman added TSM (+49%), Applied Materials (+85%), Broadcom (+25%), Meta (+12%) and Nvidia in Q1, plus a new ~$72M Intel stake; top holdings GOOGL (~$4.2B), NVDA (~$2.8B), AMZN (~$2.6B). No verifiable mid-cycle move this run.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tiger leaned hard into the AI-semis supply chain in Q1 — a stance now under pressure from the >$1trn semis drawdown and Burry's chip shorts. Carried pending the 14 Aug 13F.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: George Soros's fund held an S&P 500 put as its top position ($773M) and added NVDA, TSM and EA while cutting Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft in Q1 — a hedged, cautious posture. No new 13D/13G surfaced mid-cycle.
superInvestors.deepDive: The large index-put top holding is a portfolio hedge that looks prescient into the 28-29 Jul FOMC selloff — capturing the defensive tilt among some whales into a stretched tape. Q2 13F due 14 Aug.

superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation Trust held a concentrated ~$31.7B book (top: Berkshire, Waste Management, Canadian National, Caterpillar, Deere) with no notable individual change and no July 13D/13G filing — a low-turnover, blue-chip reference book.

A 19 Jul SEC corporate update detailed Trump Media's crypto-treasury build — ~9,542 BTC (~$593M) plus a ~$2B additional BTC purchase (~$2.6B total) — while recent DJT Form 4s are RSU grants, NOT open-market buys. The absence of any insider open-market purchase and the RSU-heavy Form 4 activity are the recent corporate developments.
